thesis: Tempus AI runs a two-sided precision-medicine platform: a genomic diagnostics lab (oncology, hereditary, MRD, cardiology AI) that generates multimodal clinical data, and a Data and Applications business that licenses that de-identified library plus AI models to pharma. Q2 2026 delivered $382.5M revenue (+22% YoY), the first GAAP profitable quarter ($5.6M, flattered by $98.5M of unrealized securities gains), $8.0M adjusted EBITDA, and ~$200M of new data bookings from AstraZeneca, GSK, Merck, BioNTech and others. FY2026 guidance is $1.595-1.605B revenue and ~$65M adjusted EBITDA, with management flagging $330-400M of annualized revenue uplift from xT and xF ADLT reimbursement pricing plus a $20B+ MRD opportunity via the pending $1.5B Personalis acquisition. The problem is price: after a 54% one-month run the stock trades at ~10x forward sales and ~24% above the $68.56 consensus target, with a 3.7 beta, ongoing GAAP losses and heavy stock-based compensation.

financials.fcf: -$245.4M (operating cash flow -$218.1M less $21.0M capex and $6.2M capitalized software)

drivers: xT ADLT pricing adds $80-100M of annualized revenue in 2027 and xF approval/pricing adds a further $250-300M, taking the 2028 uplift to ~$400M as guided on the Q2 call
Personalis closes and NeXT Personal MRD scales into Tempus' commercial footprint, attacking a management-estimated $20B+ MRD market
Data and Applications keeps compounding near 30% with 126% net revenue retention and ~$200M of quarterly bookings, dragging blended gross margin toward 70%
Oncology volume growth stays above 30% and diagnostics gross margin extends past the 62.6% posted in Q2 2026
Sustained GAAP profitability and positive free cash flow re-rate the multiple toward high-growth software rather than lab-services comparables

assumptions: FY2026 lands inside the $1.595-1.605B guide with ~$65M adjusted EBITDA; FY2027 revenue approaches the ~$1.97B consensus
Reimbursement uplift arrives but phases in over 2027-2028 rather than immediately
Personalis closes late 2026 or early 2027 with up to 50% cash funding and modest near-term dilution
Stock holds ~8-9x forward EV/sales as sell-side targets migrate up toward the market price
Stock-based compensation stays elevated (~$54M per quarter), keeping GAAP results volatile

risks: Momentum unwinds: a 3.7 beta name that ran 54% in a month mean-reverts toward the $60 50-day and $56 200-day moving averages
ADLT and xF reimbursement timing slips, so the $330-400M uplift never shows up in the modelled years
Personalis integration disappoints or MRD reimbursement stays slow, leaving $1.5B of enterprise value poorly deployed
Hereditary growth stays weak (+5% in Q2 2026) and Ambry's contribution fades as the acquisition laps
Cash burn resumes; the company carries ~$1.36B of converts and promissory notes against $820.7M of cash and securities

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results — first print after the reimbursement-driven re-rating; watch oncology volumes, MRD test count and whether FY2026 guidance moves again
Expected close of the $1.5B Personalis acquisition, including the funding mix (up to 50% cash) and any dilution
xF liquid biopsy FDA approval and ADLT pricing — management sizes this at $250-300M of annualized revenue
xT Tumor Only migration to ADLT pricing flows through tissue testing revenue, sized at $80-100M annualized
Additional pharma data-licensing and foundation-model deals following the AstraZeneca model delivery and the Recursion RNA foundation-model license
Q4 and FY2026 results plus first FY2027 guidance, the first test of the 25%+ multiyear growth claim

key_risks: Valuation and positioning — ~$15.4B market cap on ~$1.6B of 2026 revenue (~10x sales) with the $68.56 consensus target sitting ~24% below the market price
Still GAAP loss-making: the Q2 2026 profit depended on $98.5M of unrealized marketable-securities gains, while operating loss was -$75.9M
Stock-based compensation of $54.1M in Q2 2026 alone (~14% of revenue) dilutes shareholders and flatters adjusted metrics
Reimbursement risk — the bull case leans on CMS/ADLT pricing decisions and payer behaviour that Tempus does not control
Leverage: ~$1.17B of convertible senior notes plus a ~$188M convertible promissory note against $820.7M of cash and securities
Insider selling — CEO Eric Lefkofsky sold ~$16.1M of stock on 17-Sep-2026 into the rally, alongside other executive sales
Competition in genomics and MRD from Natera, Guardant Health, Foundation Medicine (Roche), Exact Sciences and Illumina
Beta of 3.7 makes the position highly sensitive to biotech and broader risk-asset drawdowns
